title: Cross field at scan scale: direct Cholesky for the aligned solve and flat-array assembly (crawfish 35 s to under 10 s)
description:
Profile 2026-10-04 (run-scene mesh-viewer --profile on load_mesh IMG_4109.glb -> repair_mesh -> cross_field(curvature_bias=-1): 469,131 vertices / 938,302 triangles): cross_field took 35.2 s. NDirectionField's own stage timers: solve aligned 25.8 s, assemble 7.2 s, populate 1.1 s, everything else about 1 s (frames, transport, rescaling 0.37 s, load vectors, hopf PCG 17 iterations 0.34 s). CPU profile: NormalMatrix.rowDot 36%, AdaptiveSolver.preconditionedConjugateGradient 11%, libjvm 29.5% (likely GC during assembly), HashMap TreeNode find/split/putTreeVal about 5%.

Cause 1: NDirectionField.solveAligned (curvature-aligned path, the one scans take) runs Jacobi-preconditioned CG from a zero start at tolerance 1e-8 with up to 5000 iterations; it needed 2089. KCP13 (Knöppel 2013, section 7) solves this with one Cholesky factorization and a back-substitution, and reports 11 s smoothing + 7 s alignment on 350k triangles on a 2013 Core 2 Duo. PARDISO Cholesky is already used by solveSmoothest through PowerIteration. Use a direct factorization for the aligned solve (desktop: PARDISO; check what the web/TeaVM build and CholeskyBackend offer and keep the web path working), with t = 0 reusing the energy matrix as now.

Cause 2: assembly builds the complex Hermitian connection Laplacian and mass matrix in Map<Long, Double> (boxed keys whose hashes collide enough to treeify buckets) and realify copies them. The sparsity pattern is the mesh's edge graph, so assemble directly into flat arrays indexed by vertex and edge (CSR or the NormalMatrix layout) with no boxing.

Requirement from the user: small models must not regress. Measure fertility (and one other small model used in benches, e.g. the rocker arm) before and after; per-stage times on small models must be no slower, within measurement noise over several runs, not just the total.
definition-of-done: 1. cross_field on the repaired crawfish (IMG_4109) under 10 s total on the desktop, with the new per-stage timings on the ticket. 2. Fertility and one other small bench model show no regression in any stage (median of at least 5 runs each, before and after, table on the ticket). 3. Same field: per-vertex angle difference against the current result below a small tolerance (state it) on fertility and the crawfish, and identical singularity counts and positions. 4. The web build (./tools/teavm-build.sh) still builds and the cross field still runs where it ran before. 5. mvn test passes.
testing-plan: 1. Baseline: run-scene mesh-viewer --profile on a scratch DSL (load_mesh, repair_mesh, cross_field) for the crawfish; same for fertility, 5 runs each. 2. After: same runs; compare stage timers and field angles (dump via a test or benchmark, not a landing debug route). 3. Unit test that flat-array assembly equals the old map assembly entry for entry on a small mesh.
changes-made: Aligned solve: NDirectionField.solveAligned factors A once (DirectSolver.factorize, AMD, through CholeskyBackend: PARDISO on desktop, EJML on web) and back-substitutes; t = 0 still reuses energyMatrix. Jacobi PCG is kept only for an open mesh with curvature_bias != 0: the bias term's boundary integral (the i/2 entries that cancel across interior edges) makes A indefinite there and Cholesky refuses it (found on a mesh_disk fixture).

Assembly: NDirectionField.assemble builds the vertex adjacency of the edge graph (one slot per distinct neighbour, so parallel edges share a slot as the keyed map did), accumulates the Hermitian entries per slot in flat arrays and realifies straight into CSR; energy and mass share rowStart/rowColumn (new public NormalMatrix CSR constructor). No Map<Long, Double>, no boxing. Unit test CrossFieldAssemblyTest keeps the old map assembly as reference and matches energy and mass matrices entry for entry with delta 0 on a torus and a disk.

Also fixed: SolverPermutation.amdOrdering packed its pattern through a boxed HashMap (TreeNode frames in the profile); now packs the symmetric adjacency straight into CSR. AMDOrdering sorts and dedupes rows itself, so the permutation is identical for every caller. PardisoCholesky sets the Intel OpenMP blocktime to 0 (kmp_set_blocktime via FFM) before each PARDISO phase: MKL's workers otherwise spin 200 ms after returning and starved the JIT, making populate 30-70% slower on small models. CholeskyBackend.preloadAsync moved to desktop startup (IxdarWindow, both paths): preloading inside cross_field overlapped and slowed its early stages (kappa 25 -> 99 ms on fertility). populate: computeTriangleIndices runs once instead of twice (stored as NDirectionField.triangleIndex), hoists the per-vertex atan2, reuses activeOfVertexId.

Timings, run-scene mesh-viewer cold JVM, median ms (min-max). Crawfish IMG_4109 repaired (469,131 V), 5 runs: assemble 7630 (7363-7978) -> 540 (528-572); solve aligned 26322 (25904-26953) -> 2107 (2001-2274); populate 798 -> 670; hopf 300 -> 276; angle rescaling 374 -> 353; kappa 160 -> 148; cross_field node 35891 (35292-36874) -> 4357 (4311-4569). Graph total incl. load+repair about 5.8 s.

Fertility (13,971 V), 7 runs before / 7 after: active-id maps 2 -> 3 (ranges 2-4 both, 1 ms timer); face frames 9 -> 9; kappa 25 -> 24; vertex frames 9 -> 8; angle rescaling 27 -> 23; assemble 203 -> 48; load vector 18 -> 18; hopf 18 -> 17; solve aligned 212 -> 144; populate 79 -> 71; cross_field node 687 -> 436. Rockerarm (35,159 V): active-id 3 -> 3; face frames 20 -> 20; kappa 26 -> 27 (ranges 24-33 vs 21-30); vertex frames 19 -> 15; angle rescaling 65 -> 55; assemble 520 -> 103; load vector 34 -> 29; hopf 47 -> 34; feature load 4 -> 4; solve aligned 769 -> 317; populate 163 -> 126; node 1817 -> 853. No stage slower beyond the 1 ms timer resolution.

Same field (benchmark.CrossFieldEquivalenceBenchmark, -Dbenchmark.dsl=<graph>, records <dsl>.angles from the old code and compares): per-vertex angle difference mod pi/2, tolerance 1e-3 rad. Fertility max 1.6e-7 mean 8.7e-10, 40/40 singular vertices identical; rockerarm max 1.0e-8 mean 1.3e-10, 20/20 identical; crawfish max 1.2e-5 mean 3.4e-9, 1460/1460 singular vertices identical (same vertex, same index4). Differences are the old PCG's 1e-8 residual.
Web: ./tools/teavm-build.sh OK (0 ERROR lines); WebPlatform has no native backend so any factor takes the EJML path, and cross_field stays desktopOnly as before. mvn test: 421 run, 0 failures.
